title: Pontotoc County forecast calls for upper 20s Thanksgiving morning
excerpt: Sunday’s front is expected to take daytime highs from the mid-70s to around 60 on Monday. The coldest night in the county forecast comes just before Thanksgiving.
locality: Pontotoc County, Mississippi. The Memphis forecast office provides the regional outlook.

paragraphs.text: Pontotoc County could wake up to temperatures in the upper 20s on Thanksgiving morning. The National Weather Service’s Friday forecast puts the coldest stretch overnight Wednesday, Nov. 25, followed by sunshine and a high in the mid-50s on Thanksgiving Day.

The change starts Sunday. After a high in the mid-70s, the county has a 30% chance of afternoon showers and a 40% chance of rain that evening. The Memphis forecast office expects a cold front late Sunday and says a few thunderstorms are possible across the Mid-South.

Monday’s high is forecast around 60, with upper 30s that night. Another chance of showers arrives after midnight Tuesday. The county forecast keeps rain chances at 20% Wednesday morning and evening. Forecasters say the midweek storm track is still uncertain.

For gardeners leaving town before the holiday, Mississippi State University Extension recommends moving tender potted plants into a sheltered place before a freeze. Roots in containers lose heat more readily than roots in the ground. For plants that must stay outside, Extension suggests grouping the pots and wrapping their sides to help protect the roots.
